issues.desc: CHK-001 adversarial (preflight fails → phase stays TEST, no partial-DONE metadata) and CHK-003 edge/adversarial (regression covers multi-worktree main ownership; process-fact contract intact) overlap in scope. PLAN should explicitly separate CHK-001 = production behavior under failure vs CHK-003 = test artifact + flow/process-contract assertion, so reviewer/test-coverage gate cannot accept one as evidence for the other.

Background states the failure consequence (DONE written then merge failed → partial-DONE) but does not name the current order of operations or the existing preflight surface that needs to move/expand. PLAN understanding_set should capture: what check exists today, where it runs relative to the phase=DONE write, and what additional readiness predicates (main worktree resolution, clean tree, merge-tree dry-run) are being added. Without that, decision_set risks debating preflight scope without a shared current-state baseline.

CHK-002 userSees only describes the abnormal hint (cd <actual-main-worktree> then git merge story/B-xxx). The verificationIntent.happy covers the normal main-current case but the user-visible expectation in that path is implicit. Recommend PLAN spell out the calm/no-op observable when main is already current and clean, so the test transcript can show "no extra cd hint emitted" and not just absence-of-failure.

High-risk story (priority=high, riskSignal 状态机/门禁 matched story_advance) requires decision_set with options >=2 and preMortem >=3 at PLAN. Background frames the preferred narrow-preflight direction but does not enumerate at least one alternative (e.g. write-DONE-then-rollback vs preflight-then-write vs lease-aware deferred-DONE). PLAN must surface and reject alternatives explicitly to satisfy the scope-plan gate.

CHK-003 adversarial intent ("Process fact contract remains valid and DONE gate evidence semantics are not downgraded to advisory text") is an internal-implementation observation rather than a user-observable outcome. The other two intents in CHK-003 already cover user-visible verification; consider rewording or accepting as engineering-internal acceptance.
